title: the clerical chart, batch one
audit_label: R869 clerical chart batch one audit
audit_comment: APPENDIX 3: THE CLERICAL QUICK-REFERENCE CHARTS, BATCH ONE - the D&DG walk round twenty-one, print pp. 134-135: the legend and ordering doctrine of the chart intro, and the first batch of deity rows - American Indian (9), Babylonian (8), Celtic (12) - riding the roster data file; the App 3 gap box stays open until the last chart batch lands. The chart prints landscape: the print voice is the ROTATED tesseract pass (pdfimages + PIL rotate -90, pNNN_rot_*), collated against the 1eonline L&L per-deity chart rows. The headline divergence: the print reads a female-clerics X for Druaga where the L&L voice reads male-only - pinned by print, eyeball flag.

banner.title: Appendix 3: the clerical quick-reference chart, batch one - the D&DG walk round twenty-one, print pp. 134-135: the chart doctrine (alphabetical within pantheon, most important first, guidelines only), the legend definitions, and the 29 rows of the American Indian, Babylonian and Celtic pantheons across the 13 printed columns.
banner.provenance: primary ink: the ROTATED extract/ddg tesseract pass (pNNN_rot_full.txt + pNNN_rot_tsv.tsv, pages 135-136; the second printing) - the chart prints landscape, the pass rides a PIL rotate(-90) over the pg renders (pdftoppm -r 300), committed c7ced34/97fcaac/06c35eb after two zero-byte strays (the tesseract .txt-append trap - stdout redirect is the fix); the collation voice: the 1eonline L&L per-deity chart rows (the mml.htm slug for Manannan Mac Lir). The adjudications: the Druaga female-clerics X (print over L&L male-only, eyeball flag), the sphere semicolons pinned by print (Heng, Hotoru, Ishtar, Marduk, Brigit), the Hastsezini jade green (the jode garble, L&L), the Arawn at death frequency (the fold), the Lugh Ltugh garble, and the Silvanus stray quote glyph noted. The chart carries no Arthurian block (heroes only).

bools.name: cqcQuickReferencePurpose
bools.comment: the listing is provided for quick reference when specific information about a cleric religion is needed

bools.name: cqcAlphabeticalWithinPantheon
bools.comment: deities are arranged alphabetically within their pantheon, except that the most important deity is listed first

bools.name: cqcGuidelinesOnly
bools.comment: the information presented is to be used as guidelines only - all clerics of one deity will not necessarily dress identically

bools.name: cqcRankByColor
bools.comment: rank within the temple is often differentiated by variations in color, lining or stripes

bools.name: cqcOrdainedAnytime
bools.comment: special sacrifices and holy days may be ordained at any time, at the pleasure of the temple or its deity

bools.name: cqcSphereMeaning
bools.comment: the sphere of control is the item, condition or element over which the deity exerts some measure of control (e.g. Air, Rain, The Hunt, Affairs of the Heart)

bools.name: cqcAnimalMeaning
bools.comment: the animal is the one most commonly associated with or sacred to that deity; clerics of the deity will often protect this type of animal; some deities are not associated with an animal

bools.name: cqcClericsMeaning
bools.comment: the clerics column describes whether the clerics of this deity can be male (M), female (F), or non-human (N-H)

bools.name: cqcRaimentMeaning
bools.comment: raiment is the prescribed form of adornment for a cleric of the deity (robes, headdresses, hairstyles, tattoos, makeup, physical disfigurations, ornaments, jewelry, footwear)

bools.name: cqcColorsMeaning
bools.comment: the colors column lists the colors, if any, associated with the deity or its clerics (ceremonial robes, altar drapings, candles, holy banners)

bools.name: cqcHolyDaysMeaning
bools.comment: the holy days listing gives the highest holy days associated with the deity and its worshipers; sacrifices, rituals and prayers on these days are more likely to be heard and acknowledged

bools.name: cqcAcknowledgementNotGranting
bools.comment: acknowledgement is not the same thing as granting a prayer or request

bools.name: cqcSacrificeMeaning
bools.comment: the sacrifice column lists both the frequency and the form of sacrifices expected of the worshipers of this deity, plus the grateful, repentant and begging-a-favor offerings

bools.name: cqcPlaceMeaning
bools.comment: the place of worship gives the most common locale or construction, whether natural or man-made, in which clerics of the deity gather to worship that deity

bools.name: cqcDruagaFemaleClericsPrint
bools.comment: the print reads two X marks for Druaga (male and female clerics); the L&L transcription reads male-only - pinned by print, eyeball flag (the Gawaine 112 precedent)

bools.name: cqcSphereSemicolonsPrint
bools.comment: the print uses semicolons in the multi-word spheres (Heng thunder; weather, Hotoru wind; weather, Ishtar love; war, Marduk cities; weather, Brigit fire; poetry) where the L&L transcription normalizes to commas

bools.name: cqcHastseziniJadeGreen
bools.comment: the Hastsezini jode green print garble reads jade green (the L&L voice)

bools.name: cqcArawnAtDeath
bools.comment: the Arawn frequency reads at death (the psm-4 fold merged the two words)

bools.name: cqcNoArthurianRows
bools.comment: the chart carries no Arthurian block - the Arthurian section is heroes-only, no deities (the batch order runs American Indian, Babylonian, Celtic)

bools.name: cqcSilvanusStrayQuote
bools.comment: the Silvanus tree planting cell carries a stray quote glyph on the print (noted, not pinned)
